label: Marigold & Ivy
description: Deep ivy green, marigold saffron and warm petal ivory. Botanical and festive without being bridal-pink — suits flower decorators, florists, event florals, nurseries, garden studios and organic brands.
notes:
Tokens only — sections never hardcode colours, they read these as CSS variables.

PALETTE LOGIC: the two colours a flower business actually works in — stem and leaf (deep ivy #1D4B3A) against marigold (#E8A33D) — over a warm petal ivory rather than a cold white. Every other warm theme in this set is red, maroon, rose or terracotta, and the only other greens are sage-linen (a much lighter, greyer sage with a tan accent) and graphite-emerald (charcoal primary, emerald only as an accent). This is the sole theme where a saturated botanical green is the PRIMARY, which is what keeps flower-decoration from looking like a second wedding template.

CONTRAST: every pair was measured, not eyeballed. Body text on bg 15.09:1, white on primary 9.91:1, white on secondary 5.60:1, text on accent 7.22:1, primary on bg 9.60:1, muted on bg 4.90:1 — all above WCAG AA 4.5:1. Muted is deliberately darker than most themes in this set (velvet-rose sits at 2.92:1, copper-ridge at 3.45:1) because it carries meta lines like prices and timings. Accent-on-bg is 2.09:1, which is FINE and matches the house pattern (every light theme here is 2.1–3.1) — `accent` is a fill colour with dark text on top of it, never body text on the background. Keep it that way if you retune it.

FONTS: Bodoni Moda (headings) + DM Sans (body). Neither is used by any other theme. IMPORTANT — the renderer requests `wght@400;500;600;700` for both families in one css2 call, so a face must actually SERVE those weights or headings silently fall back to 400 and look thin at 600/700. Prata, Gilda Display, Italiana and DM Serif Display all serve 400 only and were rejected for this reason; Bodoni Moda and DM Sans both serve all four. Verify with `curl` on the css2 URL and grep the font-weight rules before swapping either font.

Changing `primary` here restyles every section, every page, instantly.
